# Claude Agent SDK: Cost Tracking Analysis

How to get cost information out of the Claude Agent SDK (formerly Claude Code
SDK) — the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` npm package / `claude-agent-sdk`
Python package. Every factual claim traces to a source in
[citations.md](citations.md). Two independent review agents audit this output.

## Methodology

Research conducted April 2026 across four dimensions:

1. **SDK API surface for cost data** — return types, fields, scoping model
2. **Streaming events and real-time usage** — event-based cost tracking
3. **Token accounting model** — token categories, pricing, cost computation
4. **Implementation patterns** — practical code for extraction and aggregation

Sources were drawn from official Anthropic documentation (Tier 2), GitHub
issues (Tier 4), and community tools (Tier 4). All sources were fetched
in-session via WebFetch or the `gh` CLI. See [citations.md](citations.md)
for the complete source list with quality tiers.

---

## 1. SDK Identity and Package Names

The SDK was renamed from "Claude Code SDK" to "Claude Agent SDK" [5][7].
If you are currently using `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (TypeScript) or
`claude-code-sdk` (Python), you should migrate to the new package names [7]:

| Language | Old Package | New Package |
|----------|------------|-------------|
| TypeScript | `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` [7] |
| Python | `claude-code-sdk` | `claude-agent-sdk` [7] |

The rename introduced no changes to cost or usage field names [7]. The only
breaking type rename was `ClaudeCodeOptions` → `ClaudeAgentOptions` in
Python [7].

## 2. Where Cost Data Lives

### The Three Levels

The SDK scopes cost data at three levels [1]:

| Level | What It Is | Where Cost Appears |
|-------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Step** | Single model request/response | `AssistantMessage.usage` (per-step tokens) [1] |
| **`query()` call** | One invocation spanning multiple steps | `ResultMessage.total_cost_usd` (authoritative total) [1] |
| **Session** | Multiple `query()` calls linked via `resume` | **No SDK-provided total** — caller must accumulate [1] |

### The Result Message

Every `query()` call emits exactly one result message as its final message [1].
This is the authoritative cost container:

| Field | TypeScript | Python | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|--------|---------|
| Total USD cost | `total_cost_usd: number` | `total_cost_usd: float \| None` | Cumulative cost for the call [1] |
| Aggregate tokens | `usage: NonNullableUsage` | `usage: dict` | Token counts across all steps [1] |
| Per-model breakdown | `modelUsage: { [model]: ModelUsage }` | `model_usage: dict` | Per-model tokens and cost [1] |

Cost data is present on **both success and error** result subtypes [1].
Error subtypes include `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`,
`error_max_budget_usd`, and `error_max_structured_output_retries` [3].

### Per-Model Granularity

The `modelUsage`/`model_usage` map provides per-model cost via the `costUSD`
field [1][3]. This is useful when subagents run on different models:

```typescript
for (const [modelName, usage] of Object.entries(message.modelUsage)) {
  console.log(`${modelName}: $${usage.costUSD.toFixed(4)}`);
  console.log(`  Input: ${usage.inputTokens}, Output: ${usage.outputTokens}`);
  console.log(`  Cache read: ${usage.cacheReadInputTokens}`);
  console.log(`  Cache write: ${usage.cacheCreationInputTokens}`);
  console.log(`  Web searches: ${usage.webSearchRequests}`);
}
```
[1]

## 3. Token Categories

Four token categories are tracked [1][3][4]:

| Category | Aggregate Field | ModelUsage Field | Pricing Multiplier |
|----------|----------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Input | `input_tokens` | `inputTokens` | 1× base [8] |
| Output | `output_tokens` | `outputTokens` | Varies by model [8] |
| Cache creation (5m TTL) | `cache_creation_input_tokens` | `cacheCreationInputTokens` | 1.25× base input [8] |
| Cache creation (1hr TTL) | `cache_creation_input_tokens` | `cacheCreationInputTokens` | 2× base input [8] |
| Cache read | `cache_read_input_tokens` | `cacheReadInputTokens` | 0.1× base input [8] |

The SDK also tracks `webSearchRequests` in `ModelUsage`, billed at $10/1,000
searches [8]. Additionally, tool use adds overhead tokens per turn (346 tokens
for `auto`/`none` mode, 313 tokens for `any`/`tool` mode on Claude 4.x and
Sonnet 3.7+) [8]. These overhead tokens are included in the input token count.

**Naming convention split:** Aggregate `usage` uses snake_case
(`input_tokens`), while `ModelUsage`/`model_usage` uses camelCase
(`inputTokens`) — even in Python [3][4].

### Automatic Prompt Caching

The Agent SDK automatically applies prompt caching without configuration [1].
Cache creation tokens are charged at a higher rate than standard input; cache
read tokens at a reduced rate [1][8]. Track these separately from
`input_tokens` to understand caching savings [1].

## 4. The Deduplication Requirement

When Claude uses multiple tools in parallel within a single step, it emits
multiple `AssistantMessage` objects that share the same message ID with
identical usage data [1]. If you sum per-step usage without deduplicating
by ID, you will overcount.

```typescript
const seenIds = new Set<string>();
// ...
if (!seenIds.has(message.message.id)) {
  seenIds.add(message.message.id);
  totalInputTokens += message.message.usage.input_tokens;
}
```
[1]

The `total_cost_usd` on `ResultMessage` is always correct regardless of
deduplication [1]. If you only need the total, skip per-step tracking
entirely and read the result message [1].

## 5. Streaming and Real-Time Cost

By default, the SDK yields complete messages only [2]. Enable streaming
with `includePartialMessages: true` (TS) / `include_partial_messages=True`
(Python) to receive `StreamEvent` objects containing raw API events [2].

### What Streams

| Event Type | Content | Has Usage? |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| `content_block_delta` (text_delta) | Text chunks | No [2] |
| `content_block_delta` (input_json_delta) | Tool input chunks | No [2] |
| `message_delta` | Stop reason, usage | **Yes** [2] |

The `message_delta` event carries per-step usage data [2], but the SDK
documentation does not enumerate the exact fields — they are inherited from
the Claude API streaming protocol [2].

### Streaming Does Not Provide Running Totals

`StreamEvent` objects do not aggregate across steps [2]. For the call-level
total, you must still read `ResultMessage.total_cost_usd` [1]. There is no
built-in mechanism for a running cost total during execution.

### Streaming Limitations

- Incompatible with extended thinking (`maxThinkingTokens`) — no
  `StreamEvent` messages are emitted when thinking is enabled [2]
- Structured output appears only in `ResultMessage.structured_output`,
  not as streaming deltas [2]

## 6. Budget Enforcement

The `query()` options accept a maximum budget [3][4]:

```typescript
// TypeScript
query({ prompt: "...", options: { maxBudgetUsd: 1.00 } })

// Python
ClaudeAgentOptions(max_budget_usd=1.00)
```

When exceeded, the result message has `subtype: "error_max_budget_usd"` [3].
Cost data is still available on the error result [1]. This is the only
built-in spend control — there is no callback when cost approaches the
threshold.

## 7. Subagent Cost Attribution

`modelUsage` aggregates tokens across all models used in a `query()` call,
**including subagent models** [6]. It is keyed by model name, not by
subagent identity [6].

**There is no per-subagent cost breakdown available via the SDK API** [6][9][10].

GitHub issues #10388 [9] and #22625 [10] confirm this is a known gap, both
auto-closed due to inactivity without implementation. A community workaround parses JSONL session logs in
`~/.claude/projects/`, but messages are not tagged with agent ID, making exact
attribution impossible without session isolation [10][12].

**Workaround:** Isolate subagents to separate `query()` calls and track each
call's `total_cost_usd` independently. This sacrifices the SDK's built-in
subagent orchestration but provides per-agent cost visibility.

## 8. Known Issues

### Cost Calculation Discrepancies

At least one user reported a significant gap between manually calculated cost
and the SDK's reported `total_cost_usd` [11]. For a Sonnet 4.5 session with
2.3M cache read tokens, the reported cost was $3.10 vs an expected $1.87 [11].
The issue was closed as a duplicate without formula clarification [11].

Possible explanations:
- 1-hour cache writes (2× rate) vs 5-minute cache writes (1.25× rate) [8]
- Vertex AI platform pricing differs from direct Anthropic API pricing [8]
- Tool use overhead tokens or other undocumented components

The `total_cost_usd` formula is not published. Treat it as authoritative for
billing purposes, but be aware that manual verification may not match.

### Max/Pro Subscriber Visibility

The `/cost` CLI command excludes Max/Pro subscribers, showing zero usage
data [9]. This is a CLI limitation — the SDK's `ResultMessage.total_cost_usd`
is not affected.

## 9. Summary of What's Available vs. What's Missing

| Capability | Status | Source |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Total cost per `query()` call | Available via `total_cost_usd` | [1] |
| Per-model cost breakdown | Available via `modelUsage[model].costUSD` | [1][3] |
| Per-step token counts | Available via `AssistantMessage.usage` | [1] |
| Cache token tracking | Available (4 separate fields) | [1][3][4] |
| Budget enforcement | Available via `maxBudgetUsd` | [3][4] |
| Cost on error results | Available (all error subtypes) | [1][3] |
| Session-level cost total | **Not available** — must accumulate manually | [1] |
| Per-subagent cost breakdown | **Not available** — aggregated by model only | [6][9][10] |
| Real-time running cost total | **Not available** — only per-step via streaming | [2] |
| `total_cost_usd` formula | **Not published** | [11] |
| Spend threshold callbacks | **Not available** — only hard cap via budget | [3] |
